draft.title: Homeostasis
card: Homeostasis is the body keeping its internal conditions steady, even when the outside world changes. Body temperature and blood glucose (sugar) are two examples.
Cells work best within a narrow range of conditions. If temperature or glucose drifts too far from that range, cells can stop working properly.
The body uses negative feedback. A receptor detects a change, and the body responds in a way that reverses the change and brings the condition back towards normal.
For example, if the body gets too hot, sweating and wider skin blood vessels help it lose heat. If it gets too cold, shivering helps it make heat.
draft.remember: Homeostasis keeps conditions steady by using feedback that reverses a change.

opts: Keeping internal conditions steady as the outside changes
Keeping the outside environment the same as the body
Making the body's conditions rise as far as they can
Sending messages from the brain to the muscles
a.why: Homeostasis is about keeping the body's internal conditions steady. It does not control the outside environment, and the aim is a steady range, not a maximum.
a.clue: Think of what stays the same inside while the outside changes.

b.q: Sam runs on a hot day and his body temperature starts to rise. His skin sweats and his skin blood vessels widen. How do these responses show homeostasis?
opts: They reverse the rise and bring temperature back to normal
They raise his temperature further so cells work faster
They keep the outside air at a steady temperature
They stop his receptors from detecting the change
b.why: Sweating and wider blood vessels help the body lose heat, so they reverse the rise. This is negative feedback. Making the change bigger would move the body further from its normal range.
b.clue: Does the response push the change further or undo it?

a.best: Keeping internal conditions steady as the outside changes

b.best: They reverse the rise and bring temperature back to normal
